channel.title: KORTEX Blog
channel.description: Practical articles on Generative Engine Optimization, AI answer engines and entity-first content, and how one source becomes a month of cited content.

item.title: Agency, in-house team or AI studio: how to choose a content model
item.description: What each option really buys, a cost model with every figure labeled as an assumption, when each one is the better choice, and the questions to ask before you sign.

item.title: Entity SEO for founders: say who you are the same way everywhere
item.description: How a founder makes the company, the author and the method easy for machines to identify: one spelling, a real byline, matching markup and a ten-minute audit.

item.title: GEO in French and Arabic: be cited in the language your buyer asks in
item.description: How to make a site citable in French and Arabic: separate URLs, correct hreflang, native writing instead of machine translation, stable entity names and per-language measurement.

item.title: The human QA layer: what a person checks before anything ships
item.description: Why an editor reviews every AI-assisted asset, the eight things they check against your source, what they leave alone, and how the review should show on the page.

item.title: From podcast episode to authority: what one conversation can become
item.description: How to turn a podcast episode into pages that AI engines and buyers can read: choosing the episode, extracting opinions and questions, and building assets that keep the proof.

item.title: Seven repurposing mistakes that quietly weaken your authority
item.description: Repurposing one source into many assets can strengthen your expertise or dilute it. Seven mistakes to avoid, what Google says about the risky ones, and the fix for each.

item.title: GEO vs SEO for B2B: what changed and what did not
item.description: Google says optimizing for its AI features is still SEO. What that means for B2B teams, what is genuinely different, and where the GEO advice is unproven.

item.title: How to get your brand cited by ChatGPT, Perplexity and Gemini
item.description: A practical playbook for getting your brand cited in AI answers, with each step labelled as documented by an engine or as our own practice.

item.title: llms.txt: what it is, what we know, what is hype, and what we do
item.description: What llms.txt is, what its author claims, what Google says about it, and how we run one on this site without treating it as a ranking lever.

item.title: How to measure AI citations without a tool budget
item.description: A repeatable monthly method to track whether ChatGPT, Perplexity and Gemini cite you: a fixed prompt list, a simple log, Search Console and one rule for reading it.

item.title: The schema markup worth adding, and what it will not do
item.description: Which schema.org types we add to a B2B site, what Google says about structured data and AI features, and why the FAQ rich result no longer matters.

item.title: One webinar into a month of content: the pipeline, step by step
item.description: The pipeline we use to turn one webinar into linked pages, step by step, with the quality gates that stop it from turning into thin, repetitive content.

item.title: A practical guide to answer engine visibility
item.description: Answer engine visibility means being cited by ChatGPT, Perplexity and Gemini. Learn how they pick sources and the content architecture that earns citations.

item.title: How to build a category in the age of AI search.
item.description: Category creation in AI search means publishing a precise, retrievable definition before ChatGPT or Perplexity writes one for you. A 4-phase B2B playbook.

item.title: The B2B content audit framework for AI retrieval readiness.
item.description: A GEO content audit scores every page on 5 criteria AI answer engines reward, then sorts it into keep, retrofit or retire. Framework, scorecard and checklist.

item.title: Entity-first content: the architecture AI search rewards.
item.description: Entity-first content builds one consistent knowledge graph that ChatGPT, Perplexity and Gemini can cluster and cite. The 5 components, linking rules and schema.

item.title: Why most B2B LinkedIn content dies in 48 hours.
item.description: B2B LinkedIn posts fade within two days because they are published as one-off activity. How to link each post to answer pages that keep working for months.

item.title: The new B2B content stack: video, entities, answers, distribution.
item.description: The B2B content stack in four layers: raw signal, entities, answer assets, distribution. How to run each, which AI tools to use, and why the old stack fails.

item.title: From one video to 30 days of content AI engines can cite
item.description: Turn one video into 30 days of linked content: pillar article, FAQ page, comparison page and LinkedIn posts. The extraction method, step by step.

item.title: Ranking is not enough. Become the source AI answers cite.
item.description: GEO vs SEO explained: how to structure B2B content so ChatGPT, Perplexity and Gemini cite your company as the source, with a five-step page framework.
